data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A panel of non-experts following a checklist is more reliable than a single expert because the checklist enforces a 'search breadth' that overrides the expert's 'premature closure' bias.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The task requires synthesis of non-linear dependencies not captured in the checklist","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The checklist is too coarse, leading to 'blind compliance' where the panel ignores obvious anomalies not on the list","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The checklist acts as a cognitive forcing function that mandates the evaluation of low-probability but high-impact variables which an expert's intuitive heuristic (pattern matching) typically skips once a high-probability match is found.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
